items.stem:
Analyze the following two primary source excerpts and construct a document-based argument about how the GI Bill transformed American society in the postwar period — and who was excluded from its benefits.

DOCUMENT A: Excerpt from the Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944 (GI Bill of Rights), June 22, 1944 (U.S. Statutes at Large, 1944; National Archives, public domain):
"Any person who shall have served in the active military or naval service of the United States on or after September 16, 1940, and prior to the termination of the present war, and who shall have been discharged or released therefrom under conditions other than dishonorable, after active service of ninety days or more... shall be eligible for and entitled to receive education or training under this part... Loans for the purchase or construction of homes, farms, and business property..."

DOCUMENT B: Excerpt from the Executive Order 8802, President Franklin D. Roosevelt, June 25, 1941 (Federal Register, Vol. 6, No. 125, June 25, 1941; National Archives, archives.gov):
"We call upon the President and Congress to declare racial democracy here at home as our war aim, even as we fight for democracy abroad... We must have a victory at home as well as abroad... Shall we suffer Jim Crow to continue unchallenged?"

Using HIPP analysis for each document and your knowledge of the GI Bill's implementation and postwar America, construct an argument that evaluates: (1) the transformative economic and social impact of the GI Bill on the white middle class; (2) how racial discrimination in the GI Bill's administration — through local VA offices, segregated universities, and discriminatory lending — denied many African American veterans the bill's promised benefits; (3) how this gap between the bill's text (Document A) and its discriminatory implementation connects to Executive Order 8802 and the Fair Employment Practices Committee's warning (Document B). Include at least two pieces of outside evidence.
items.stemEs:
Analiza los siguientes dos extractos de fuentes primarias y construye un argumento basado en documentos sobre cómo el GI Bill transformó la sociedad estadounidense en el período de posguerra — y quién fue excluido de sus beneficios.

DOCUMENTO A: Extracto de la Ley de Reajuste de los Militares en Servicio de 1944 (GI Bill of Rights), 22 de junio de 1944 (Estatutos de los EE.UU., 1944; Archivo Nacional, dominio público):
"Cualquier persona que haya servido en el servicio militar o naval activo de los Estados Unidos en o después del 16 de septiembre de 1940, y antes de la terminación de la guerra actual, y que haya sido dado de baja o liberado del mismo bajo condiciones que no sean deshonrosas, después de un servicio activo de noventa días o más... será elegible y tendrá derecho a recibir educación o capacitación bajo esta parte... Préstamos para la compra o construcción de viviendas, granjas y propiedades comerciales..."

DOCUMENTO B: Extracto del editorial de la Campaña Doble V, Pittsburgh Courier, 14 de febrero de 1942 (Pittsburgh Courier, 1942; dominio público):
"Pedimos al Presidente y al Congreso que declaren la democracia racial aquí en casa como nuestro objetivo de guerra, al mismo tiempo que luchamos por la democracia en el extranjero... Debemos tener una victoria en casa así como en el extranjero... ¿Permitiremos que el Jim Crow continúe sin ser desafiado?"

Usando el análisis HIPP para cada documento y tu conocimiento sobre la implementación del GI Bill y la América de posguerra, construye un argumento que evalúe: (1) el impacto económico y social transformador del GI Bill en la clase media blanca; (2) cómo la discriminación racial en la administración del GI Bill — a través de las oficinas locales de la VA, universidades segregadas y préstamos discriminatorios — negó a muchos veteranos afroamericanos los beneficios prometidos por la ley; (3) cómo esta brecha entre el texto del proyecto de ley (Documento A) y su implementación discriminatoria se conecta con la advertencia de la Campaña Doble V (Documento B). Incluye al menos dos piezas de evidencia externa.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response will: (1) Apply full HIPP to both documents. Document A — Historical context: WWII service and the need to reintegrate millions of veterans; Intended audience: Congress and the American public; Purpose: Create a universal entitlement for veterans; Point of view: Neutral statutory language that is race-blind on its face but implemented through racially segregated institutions. Document B — Historical context: African Americans serving in a segregated military while facing Jim Crow at home; Intended audience: the Black community and sympathetic white readers; Purpose: Demand racial equity as a war aim; Point of view: Black press challenging the contradiction of fighting for democracy abroad while facing oppression at home. (2) Argue that the GI Bill's race-neutral language was systematically subverted: local VA administrators steered Black veterans away from loans; HBCUs lacked capacity for the surge in student veterans; all-white neighborhoods used restrictive covenants to block Black homeownership. (3) Connect to outside evidence: segregated military (Executive Order 9981 not until 1948); Tuskegee Airmen's postwar inequality; the wealth gap between white and Black veterans persisting into the 1950s–60s; the Double V Campaign's prediction of betrayal vindicated. (4) Strong responses will connect to the Civil Rights Movement (US.71) as a direct consequence of this postwar betrayal — soldiers who fought for democracy returned to demand it at home.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.57, US.53 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Sophisticated thesis connecting the GI Bill's promise versus its racially discriminatory implementation. Full HIPP for both documents including critical analysis of Document A's race-neutral language and Document B's predictive warning. Three or more outside evidence pieces. Explicit synthesis connecting US.57 (GI Bill) to US.53 (Double V/African American service) and forward to US.71 (Civil Rights). Command of historical reasoning (continuity/change over time, causation).
5 - Advanced: Clear thesis. Both documents with mostly complete HIPP. Two or more outside pieces. Clear connection between postwar betrayal and Civil Rights Movement.
4 - Proficient: Clear thesis. Both documents with three or more HIPP elements each. One outside piece. Some connection to postwar racial inequality.
3 - Adequate: Thesis present. One document fully analyzed with HIPP. Some outside evidence. Limited synthesis.
2 - Developing: Documents described but not analytically connected. Minimal outside evidence.
1 - Beginning: One document referenced without HIPP. No synthesis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Document A — race-neutral statutory language; 'conditions other than dishonorable' is significant because Black servicemen were disproportionately given less-than-honorable discharges, disqualifying them. Document B — 'Jim Crow' reference signals that the Double V editorial writers anticipated the very betrayal that the GI Bill would represent.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Segregated military units; HBCU enrollment limits; restrictive covenants; VA loan discrimination in the South; Shelley v. Kraemer (1948); suburbanization as a whites-only phenomenon; Black veterans' unemployment rates post-WWII; Executive Order 9981 desegregating the military (1948) as partial, belated victory.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada que conecta la promesa del GI Bill con su implementación racialmente discriminatoria. HIPP completo para ambos documentos, incluyendo análisis crítico del lenguaje racialmente neutral del Documento A y la advertencia predictiva del Documento B. Tres o más piezas de evidencia externa. Síntesis explícita que conecta US.57 (GI Bill) con US.53 (Doble V/servicio afroamericano) y hacia adelante con US.71 (Derechos Civiles). Dominio del razonamiento histórico.
5 - Avanzado: Tesis clara. Ambos documentos con HIPP mayormente completo. Dos o más piezas externas. Conexión clara entre la traición de posguerra y el Movimiento de Derechos Civiles.
4 - Competente: Tesis clara. Ambos documentos con tres o más elementos HIPP. Una pieza externa. Conexión con la desigualdad racial de posguerra.
3 - Adecuado: Tesis presente. Un documento completamente analizado con HIPP. Alguna evidencia externa. Síntesis limitada.
2 - En desarrollo: Documentos descritos pero no conectados analíticamente. Evidencia externa mínima.
1 - Inicial: Un documento referenciado sin HIPP. Sin síntesis.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DE DOCUMENTOS: Documento A — 'condiciones que no sean deshonrosas' es significativo porque a los soldados negros se les daban descargas menos que honorables de forma desproporcionada. Documento B — la referencia al 'Jim Crow' señala que los editorialistas anticiparon la traición que el GI Bill representaría.
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Unidades militares segregadas; límites de matrícula en HBCUs; convenios restrictivos; discriminación en préstamos de la VA; Shelley v. Kraemer (1948); suburbanización como fenómeno exclusivo para blancos; tasas de desempleo de veteranos negros; Orden Ejecutiva 9981 (1948).
